title: Follow along: one customer question becomes five pieces
goal: Turn one lesson from the week into a post, a video script, an email, a website answer and a Google post. Find the weakest one, fix only that one, and approve what is ready.
you_need: This demo, open in a browser
An AI chat you are signed in to (Claude or ChatGPT)
Optional: one question a customer asked you this week, and three things you wrote yourself

steps.do: Open the demo (double-click Launch) and click Week 5.
steps.see: Step 1, This week's idea: a customer's question about planting in the fall, a list of facts and three writing samples.
steps.tip: Everything here is made up. Your own words never leave your browser.

steps.do: Read step 1 like the owner. Find the crew's last planting day in the facts, then read the three writing samples out loud.
steps.see: Saturday, November 21, and three short pieces that sound like one person.
steps.tip: The samples are how the AI learns the voice. A text, an email and an old post are enough.

steps.do: In step 2, find the rules inside the prompt. Press Copy the prompt and the material, paste it into your AI chat and send.
steps.see: The rules: use only the facts I gave you, no invented numbers, reviews or promises, never name a customer, write like the samples.
steps.tip: This is the new-hire rule again: the job, the context, the rules, an example. The check is you.

steps.do: Copy the AI's whole answer, paste it into step 3 and press Use this answer.
steps.see: Five cards in step 4, each with a word count: a post, a video script, an email, a website answer and a Google post.
steps.tip: No AI chat handy? Use the button that loads the sample answer.

steps.do: Read the five cards. On the weakest one, press This one is weakest. In step 5, type what is wrong with it and press Copy the follow-up. Send it to the AI, paste the fixed piece back and press Replace this piece.
steps.see: The card in step 4 shows the new text and a badge that says fixed.
steps.tip: In the sample answer, the Google Business Profile post promises a guarantee. No fact says that.

steps.do: In step 6, tick Approve for each piece you would put your name on. Press Copy the approved pieces.
steps.see: A badge counts the approved pieces, and only those are copied.
steps.tip: Scheduling is not approving. Read the whole piece first.

steps.do: In step 7, tick Monday and Tuesday. In step 8, type this week's number and press Add this week.
steps.see: 20 of 60 budgeted minutes ticked off, and a new bar in the chart.
steps.tip: The hour is a budget, not a promise. The number is measured. Why it moved is your best guess.

steps.see: A new number on your one screen: pieces approved this week.
steps.tip: Next Wednesday: what happens when those new people get in touch.

real_life: Tonight: press Clear the sample and type my own idea. Write down one question a customer asked you this week, in their words, with a few true facts and three things you wrote yourself. Leave out anything private about a customer.
Run the prompt on it, with the word landscaping changed to your own business. Approve the best piece and schedule it for tomorrow, or set a reminder and post it by hand.
On Friday, write down one number: how many new people got in touch this week. Press Clear the log first, then add your own.
if_it_breaks: The AI is slow or down: load the sample answer in step 3 and keep going. Step 5 has a sample fix for the Google Business Profile post too. The lesson is the checking and the approving, not the typing.
The five cards do not appear: each piece has to start with its own line, PIECE 1: to PIECE 5:. Step 3 shows a line to send the AI that asks for that shape.
Start over with the sample data puts everything back.
